title: Console walkthrough: usage analytics & cost breakdown - Solaris Health
summary: Maya and Samir ran a console walkthrough focused on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdowns. Customer wanted clarity on how Redwood surfaces per-route cost, token-level billing, and how caching/batching impacts unit economics. Security questions around KMS, retention, and SSO were raised. Agreed next steps: send pilot pricing, share security package, schedule a 1-week POC benchmark run with sample traffic.
next_steps: Maya: send pilot pricing and Dedicated capacity options - due 2025-12-05
Samir: share quickstart benchmark spreadsheet + template traffic - due 2025-12-06
Maya & Alicia: schedule POC kickoff (1-week benchmark) - target week of 2025-12-15
Samir: send SSO/SAML setup doc and SOC2 summary - due 2025-12-04
action_items: Maya Chen; Prepare pricing sheet (hosted vs dedicated) + estimated monthly unit costs based on their 1M monthly tokens; Due: 2025-12-05
Samir Patel; Provide benchmark spreadsheet and sample k6 script for traffic replay; Due: 2025-12-06
Priya Narayanan; Share internal compliance checklist and list of vendors for SOC2 items (informational); Due: 2025-12-07
transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2025-12-03 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~47m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Samir Patel (Redwood SE); Jordan Voss (Redwood Product) -- Alicia Gomez (Solaris Head of ML); Marcus Lee (Platform Eng); Priya Narayanan (Security); Ethan Zhao (PM)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on this account, and Samir our SE will run the console. Quick intro?
[00:08] Alicia: Hi all, Alicia here. We're evaluating Redwood for inference on a patient-intake assistant and some triage routing. We're particularly interested in how you surface cost per route.
[00:20] Samir: Great, thanks Alicia. I'll share my screen and start in the console - a quick note, some of the auto-transcript might spell KV cache as K-V cache or K V, sorry for that
[00:30] Samir: (screen share) Alright, this is the Usage Analytics landing — top-level metrics: tokens in/out, request counts, average latency, and cost. You can filter by model, route, and time window.
[01:05] Marcus: Can you show per-route breakdown? We have an intake route and a follow-up summarization route, we need per-route SLAs and cost.
[01:12] Samir: Yep. Click on Routes -> Per-route dashboard. Here we have route-level time series for qps, p95 latency, tokens per request, and an estimated cost column that rolls up token-unit cost and any infra surcharge.
[01:30] Samir: Notice over here, the cost calculation uses your configured pricing profile - for hosted it's token-unit pricing; for dedicated it's commit-based with an overlay for burst. We also show open/closed intervals where caching reduced tokens.
[01:48] Alicia: That estimated cost — does it include the effect of KV cache hits or prefix caching?
[01:52] Samir: Good question. Yes, the console shows 'effective tokens' after cache hits. If you enable prefix/KV caching we display both raw tokens requested and effective billed tokens. There's a toggle to view savings over time so you can see how many tokens the cache avoided.
[02:20] Ethan: How granular is the token attribution? Is it per user session or per request ID?
[02:25] Samir: Right now attribution is per request ID and we have an optional session-level aggregation you can enable. That helps when you do multi-turn conversations so the KV cache reuse is reflected across the session.
[02:40] Marcus: What about streaming calls? We do some streaming in the triage flow. Does the console show streaming token breakdown?
[02:46] Samir: Streaming is supported. We show initial prompt tokens, delta tokens, and finalization tokens. Cost column sums them; there is also per-chunk latency visualization for debugging.
[03:05] Alicia: Can you pull up an example route with optimization recommendations?
[03:10] Samir: Sure. We'll open the Optimize suggestions panel. For this route we recommend increasing batch size from 8 to 16 off-peak and enabling 8-bit quantization on the LLM variant. We show estimated savings: approx 22% token-cost reduction and a 15% throughput boost in our profiler.
[03:35] Alicia: Is the quantization recommendation safe for our NER/safety prompts? We cannot degrade accuracy on some intents.
[03:42] Samir: We have a caution flag — the console will show you a quality delta estimate based on Redwood's eval harness against your provided prompt set. For safety-critical intents we recommend running the POC benchmark (we give a per-prompt regression alert). You can pin a non-quantized model for those specific routes.
[04:05] Priya: From a security perspective, how is customer data handled in hosted mode? We need to know retention and key management.
[04:12] Maya: Good callout. For hosted we offer configurable retention windows; default is 30 days but we can set to 0 retention for specific accounts. KMS integration is supported for encrypting at-rest; we can rotate keys and provide audit logs. We'll share the SOC2 summary and KMS integration guide after this call.
[04:38] Priya: And for Private or Dedicated — do you support bring-your-own-KMS and HSM?
[04:42] Samir: Yes — Private deployments can be configured with customer-managed KMS endpoints and HSMs in the VPC. We also export audit logs to your SIEM via S3 or a syslog sink.
[05:00] Marcus: Back to cost: how do you calculate the infra surcharge you mentioned? We have spikes where GPU utilization goes up.
[05:07] Samir: Infra surcharge is a simple amortized overlay to account for reserved GPU pools or burst GPU credits when on Dedicated. In hosted, it's baked into per-token price; in Dedicated, the console shows your baseline commit cost and then a per-token marginal when you burst beyond commit. You can also set automatic fallbacks to cheaper model variants if latency allows.
[05:35] Alicia: Can we set custom dashboards for engineering vs product teams?
[05:40] Samir: Yep — dashboards are role-aware. We have templates: finance, infra, product. Finance shows spend by route and by business unit, infra shows utilization and tail latencies. RBAC controls let you assign who sees cost details.
[05:56] Ethan: If we want to do canary rollout, can the console show cost delta between canary and baseline automatically?
[06:03] Samir: You can create a rollout and Redwood will track both performance and cost side-by-side; it surfaces a delta report and alerts if cost or error rate exceeds thresholds.
[06:20] Alicia: I'd like to run a 1-week POC with our intake traffic. Can you outline what you need for that?
[06:26] Samir: We need a representative traffic dump — either sample protobufs or a k6 script to replay traffic, plus your success criteria (latency SLO, max cost per 1k tokens, quality thresholds). I'll send the benchmark spreadsheet and a k6 template after the call.
[06:45] Marcus: How easy is it to switch a route from hosted to dedicated mid-POC if we want to test both?
[06:51] Samir: It's architected to be seamless at the routing layer. You can pin a route to a deployment policy — hosted, dedicated, or hybrid. The routing logs will show the switch and we can compare cost/perf in the same dashboard.
[07:10] Priya: For compliance we'll need IP allowlists and SSO integration. Do you support SAML and SCIM?
[07:15] Maya: Yes. SAML for SSO and SCIM for provisioning. We'll send the SSO checklist. For IP allowlists we support VPC peering for Private, and IP allowlisting for Dedicated egress.
[07:30] Alicia: Any limits around model variants? We use an internal tuned variant occasionally.
[07:34] Samir: You can bring custom models in Private or Dedicated. For hosted we can host vetted variants if they pass security screening. Model version pinning is supported per-route.
[07:50] Ethan: Can the console break down spend by label or tag? We tag routes by product line and cost center.
[07:55] Samir: Yes, tags propagate through billing; you can aggregate cost by tag key. We also export a CSV or provide an API for cost queries.
[08:12] (brief crosstalk)
[08:30] Samir: Quick demo: here is the per-route timeline. See this dip — that's a cache hit spike. If I click into that window you see the KV cache hit rate and the exact token savings, plus a timeline showing which requests benefited.
[09:00] Alicia: That view is helpful. On the optimization suggestions — can you show where quality regressions are noted?
[09:07] Samir: In the suggestion pane each recommendation has a quality delta score and links to failing prompts. We also let you run an inline A/B eval between variants using your eval set.
[09:30] Marcus: Any way to estimate monthly cost at scale? We project 12M tokens/month first year.
[09:36] Maya: We'll provide a cost model in the pricing sheet; for hosted we'll show per-token tiers and an example bill; for Dedicated we'll show commit levels and an amortized per-token. We'll model the KV cache and batching savings so you can see net.
[09:55] Alicia: One more on monitoring — do you integrate with Datadog / New Relic for tracing?
[10:00] Samir: Yes — we export traces and metrics to Datadog and support OpenTelemetry. You can also enable request-level traces from the console to send to your APM.
[10:15] Ethan: On the demo route, how did you get the 22% savings figure?
[10:19] Samir: That was from profiler runs with increased batch sizes and 8-bit quantization. We ran 1000 synthetic requests and measured effective tokens and latency distribution. The profiler stores experiment configs so you can reproduce.
[10:35] Alicia: Are there any hidden costs like egress or logs retention that we should be aware of?
[10:40] Maya: Egress costs are separate only for Private deployments where you use your own cloud account; for hosted it's included in the price. Log retention beyond the default (30 days) may incur extra charge which we'll call out in the pricing sheet.
[10:58] Marcus: For Dedicated, how does autoscaling interact with committed capacity?
[11:04] Samir: Autoscaling will use your allocated GPU pool and can burst into a billing tier. The console shows commit utilization and burst events; you can set policy to auto-fallback to cheaper variants when burst is expensive.
[11:30] Alicia: Great, I think we have what we need to start. A couple of security people will review the SOC2 and KMS docs.
[11:38] Priya: I'll want the SOC2 PDF and the KMS integration guide — also sample audit logs format.
[11:44] Maya: We'll send those. Samir, anything else to demo?
[11:47] Samir: One last thing — the cost explorer supports cohort analysis so you can see cost per customer segment if you tag requests on ingestion. That may help pricing for your B2B partners.
[12:05] Alicia: Love that. OK, next steps then?
[12:10] Maya: Recap: we'll send the pricing sheet, benchmark template, SSO/SOC2 docs; Samir will share the k6 script and benchmark spreadsheet; schedule POC kickoff next week.
[12:24] Ethan: Sounds good. Thanks all.
[12:26] (meeting ends)

Notes: Transcript includes some auto-caption errors and occasional shorthand (KV cache / K V cache). Links referenced during call: https://redwood.ai/docs/console-usage (console docs), https://redwood.ai/security/soc2.pdf (SOC2 summary), https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/solaristemplate.csv (benchmark spreadsheet placeholder).
notes: Customer is leaning towards a Dedicated POC to validate tail latency under commit; security team requested SOC2+KMS docs. Finance will review pricing sheet once sent.
